merger_name: MA Financial (Redcape Fund) – Caves Coastal Bar & Bungalows

other_parties.name: MA Redcape Hotel Fund RE Limited

party_page.name: Ma Redcape Hotel Fund Re Limited

merger_description:
Redcape Hotel Group Pty Ltd and MAHF Custodian Pty Ltd as custodian for RGM TT Pty Ltd (which is the trustee for the Caves Beach Hotel Trust) (together, the **Acquirers**) propose to acquire all the freehold and strata land interests, buildings, licences and business assets (both tangible and intangible) of Caves Coastal Bar & Bungalows (the **Target**) located in NSW from entities controlled by the Oscars Hotel Group (the **Acquisition**).

The Acquirers are part of MA Financial’s Redcape Fund, which owns and operates community pubs and hotels. The Redcape Fund portfolio currently has 41 pubs and hotels in NSW, Queensland and Victoria.

The Target is a community pub and hotel offering food, beverage, accommodation, gaming, entertainment, and function and event services. It is located at 27 Mawson Close and 12A Beachside Drive, Caves Beach NSW 2281. The Target has 18 studio style accommodation bungalows and 17 gaming machine licences that will be acquired through the Acquisition. The Target also hosts a ‘Beer, Food & Wine Festival’.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the Acquisition
is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of competition given:
a) there is a small horizontal overlap between the Acquirer and
the Target in the supply of accommodation, on-premises
liquor, dining and gaming services in the local area
surrounding the Target
b) there are alternative suppliers of accommodation, on-
premises liquor, dining and gaming services in the local area
surrounding the Target.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
